entity_ranked_evidence.title: 33 Koti Devta: The Spiritual Cosmos of Hinduism
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: ## 33 Koti Devta: The Spiritual Cosmos of Hinduism. The concept of 33 koti devta is one of the most profound and often misunderstood aspects of Hindu theology. In many ancient Hindu scriptures, "koti" is used to denote a class or category of things or beings. For example, in the context of "33 koti devta," it refers to 33 types or classes of deities, not 33 crore (330 million) individual gods. * The earliest references to the 33 koti devta are found in the ancient Vedic texts. The Rigveda, one of Hinduism’s foundational scriptures, mentions the existence of 33 principal deities, divided into three realms: The reference to 33 koti devta appears in several ancient Hindu scriptures other than Rigveda. India’s spiritual landscape is marked by diversity in worship, with countless gods and goddesses revered in various forms, names, and manifestations. The concept of 33 koti devta symbolizes the infinite manifestations of the Supreme Reality  in Hindu philosophy.
